strategies.summary: A top-down filtering framework to identify High Probability conditions characterized by clear one-sidedness and an obvious draw on liquidity, while actively avoiding Low Probability conditions (50/50 biases, post-expansion exhaustion, and pre-news consolidation).

timeframes.notes: Requires higher timeframe context (4-hour and above) to establish the obvious draw on liquidity.

other: Must take less than 10 seconds (up to 1 minute maximum) to identify the clear draw on liquidity.

glossary.Clear One-Sidedness: When you can only make arguments on one side of the market (e.g., 100% bullish, 0% bearish) with no opposing PD arrays or structure.
glossary.50/50 Bias: When both bullish and bearish arguments exist (even if weighted 70/30 or 90/10), making the market low probability.
glossary.Low Probability Conditions: A state where the odds are not heavily in your favor, commonly occurring during 50/50 biases, after major expansions hit a target, or ahead of major news.

custom_signals.name: obvious_draw_on_liquidity
custom_signals.plain_definition: A higher timeframe target (swing high/low) that is immediately recognizable within 10 seconds of opening the chart.

custom_signals.name: failed_rejection
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price sweeps a level but fails to displace immediately in the opposite direction, instead slowly climbing or dropping.

custom_signals.name: consolidation_expansion_consolidation
custom_signals.plain_definition: A 3-candle sequence where candle 1 is consolidation (or expansion), candle 2 is an expansion creating an FVG, and candle 3 is unpredictable consolidation.

custom_signals.name: major_expansion_dol_swept
custom_signals.plain_definition: A major expansion to either side that has just taken out the higher timeframe draw on liquidity.

custom_signals.name: pre_major_news
custom_signals.plain_definition: The time window on the day of a CPI, FOMC, or NFP release, prior to the actual release time.

sequence: Open the chart and apply the 10-second rule (1 minute maximum): if the draw on liquidity is not stupidly obvious immediately, do not trade [05:05].
Verify there is clear one-sidedness, meaning you can only make arguments for one direction (100% bullish/bearish, 0% opposing) [01:14].
Ensure the market is not in a low probability state: check that it is not ahead of CPI/FOMC/NFP, and not immediately after a major expansion has swept the draw on liquidity [09:09, 10:32].
Formulate an 'if/then' demand for price action based on the obvious draw [04:12].
Execute only when price delivers exactly to those demands; if you have to convince yourself, do not take the trade [03:15].

invalidation.text: If you need to convince yourself to take the trade or force the price action, the setup is invalid.
If price sweeps a level but fails to immediately reject and instead slowly climbs/drops, it becomes a 50/50 bias and is invalid.

filters.text: Do not trade ahead of CPI, FOMC, and NFP; wait until after the release.
Do not chase price or try to call a top/bottom immediately after a major expansion has taken the draw on liquidity. Wait for clear 4H+ structure.

entry_rule.text: Wait for price to deliver exactly to your pre-planned 'if/then' demands based on the obvious draw on liquidity.
entry_rule.quote: demanding something off of price and price doing exactly what you demanded

target_rule.text: Target the stupidly obvious draw on liquidity (e.g., a major swing high or low).
target_rule.quote: the draw liquidity should be so stupidly obvious

stop_rule.text: Not specified in this conceptual video.

presenter_claims.claim: In those high probability conditions you might have a win rate of maybe 80 90% with crazy returns.
If you know when to trade you are ahead of 99% of your competition.

strategies.notes: This video provides a conceptual filtering framework rather than a mechanical entry strategy. It emphasizes psychological discipline (the 10-second rule) and strict environmental filters (avoiding pre-news, post-expansion, and 50/50 conditions) to define High Probability conditions.

uncertainties.why: The video focuses entirely on market conditions (when to trade) rather than execution mechanics (how to enter).

confidence.reason: The presenter's definitions of High Probability vs Low Probability conditions, the 10-second rule, and pre-news filters are stated explicitly and repeated for clarity.

custom_signals_observed.name: failed_rejection
custom_signals_observed.presenter_calls_it: don't see a rejection lower we slowly climb higher

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps the drawn liquidity low. The presenter expects the overlapping order block and FVG to immediately reject price lower.
Instead of rejecting, price fails to follow through and slowly climbs higher, leading to seek-and-destroy conditions.
The presenter evaluates the arguments: overall bearish (70%) but failing to drop (30% bullish). This lack of 100% one-sidedness makes it a low probability 50/50 environment.

examples.presenter_commentary: He uses the Dollar chart to highlight what a 50/50 bias looks like in real time. Because price failed to aggressively reject off the PD array and instead began to chop slowly upwards, the conditions devolved into 'seek and destroy,' making it a market to avoid.
